headline: Steady quarter as pending Merck buyout moves toward close
summary_short: Bio-Techne's fiscal Q4 2026 net sales rose 1.3% y/y (3% organic) to $321.2M; GAAP EPS was $0.35 versus a $0.11 loss a year ago that included an impairment charge, while adjusted EPS slipped to $0.52 from $0.53. The company remains on track for its $73/share, ~$11.3B all-cash acquisition by Merck KGaA.
summary_long: Q4 FY26 net sales grew 1% reported (3% organic) to $321.2M, led by an 8% organic rebound in Diagnostics and Spatial Biology against a flatter 1% organic gain in Protein Sciences, whose margin slipped to 42.0% from 43.6% on unfavorable mix. GAAP operating income swung to $74.3M (23.1% margin) from a $23.9M loss (-7.5% margin) a year ago on a non-recurring impairment charge; adjusted operating margin held roughly flat at 32.2%. Adjusted EPS slipped to $0.52 from $0.53 on a $3.7M investment loss and a higher tax rate. Cash rose to $264.7M; long-term debt fell to $200.0M from $346.0M. Bio-Techne has stopped holding conference calls while its $73/share, ~$11.3B Merck KGaA acquisition proceeds; no forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: CEO Kim Kelderman cited 'improved performance and solid execution' across biopharma, research and diagnostic workflows, while the company continues progressing toward its previously announced acquisition by Merck KGaA.

3% organic growth was led by an 8% organic increase in Diagnostics and Spatial Biology, aided by the Exosome Diagnostics divestiture and volume growth; Protein Sciences organic growth was only 1%, and a divested business cut 2 points off reported growth.
GAAP operating margin was favorably impacted by a non-recurring impairment charge recorded in the year-ago quarter that did not repeat this quarter.
Adjusted operating margin was favorably impacted by profitability initiatives and the Exosome Diagnostics divestiture, partially offset by unfavorable product mix.

Adjusted EPS fell despite adjusted operating income rising 2.0% y/y because a $3.7M investment/non-operating loss (versus none a year ago) and a higher adjusted tax rate (22.3% vs 21.5%) offset the operating gain.
Net income's swing to a $54.6M profit from a $17.7M loss tracks the GAAP operating income recovery, which itself reflects the absence of last year's impairment charge.
